verdict.line: Sold out. An EC cannot be sold on before completion and can be resold only after its 5-year minimum occupation period, so later buyers will buy resales from about 2035; pay no more than about $1,930 psf in today's money. At launch: Buy. A 3-bed here at about $1,790 psf is at or below what the closest competitors' 3-bed-size resales support (about $1,840 psf as a new launch). 3-bed and 4-bed are the most wanted sizes in this own-stay family area.

compsNote: No suitable competitor within 1 km, so the nearest within 2 to 3 km are used. Only executive condos are compared (an EC sells below private condos because of its buyer rules). Near-twins come first: up to two condos within 1.5 km with a similar number of homes (half to double) completed in 2016 or later. Then every suitable condo within 1 km (same tenure, completed 2011 or later first), widening to 2 km and 3 km only if fewer than 3. Resale ECs past their 5-year minimum occupation period sell to any Singaporean or PR. Resale prices are URA medians for the last 6 months where there were at least 5 resales, otherwise the last 12 months. Condos launched before June 2023 measured their areas under the old rules (including air-con ledges), so their psf is raised 5% to compare like for like.
priceDecide: EC cap: launch prices of executive condos are held down by the $16,000 income ceiling and the 30% mortgage limit, so the buy-at is capped at the highest EC launch of the past 24 months moved to today, plus 5% (Coastal Cabana (EC), about $1,840 psf); this applies to the 3-bed, 4-bed. Like for like by size: for each unit type we take each resale competitor's average psf for units within about 15% of that size (last 6 months, or 12 or 24 if too few). Where a competitor has too few resales of a size, that size is estimated from its own nearest size, so every unit type is judged against the same competitors. Each is raised by a new-launch premium that rises with each competitor's age (37% to 40% here): launches selling now in the OCR charge about 9% over a just-completed resale and about 2.6 points more for each year of its age (30 launches against 107 of their resale competitors, this one and the 6 most extreme pairs left out). Buy at or below = the average of the competitors' new-launch equivalents for that size (a launch nearby from the last 2 years counts for half); walk away above = 5% more. 3-bed: buy at or below $1,840, walk away above $1,930, this project about $1,793 psf; 4-bed: buy at or below $1,840, walk away above $1,930, this project about $1,870 psf. This project's price by unit type follows the developer's launch 'from' prices. No developer floor can be worked out: the developers already owned the land.

exit.note: At launch an EC bought from the developer is capped by the 30% mortgage servicing ratio (MSR) and a $16,000 household income ceiling; resale buyers after the minimum occupation period face only the 55% TDSR. How we test each buyer group, in today's money (prices, HDB values and incomes tend to rise together): the unit at today's launch average price; a 25% down payment plus Buyer's Stamp Duty; HDB upgraders put their flat's sale proceeds in first (median resale price, minus an illustrative $150,000 loan). The group can buy if that capital covers the down payment and stamp duty; the income the remaining 30-year loan needs (tested at 4% under the 55% TDSR) is shown against SingStat's 2025 averages by home type, excluding employer CPF (4-room $11,097, 5-room and executive $13,887, condo $22,006). HDB resale prices rose 4.2% a year over the past 10 years, so upgraders' capital usually grows too. Singaporean HDB owners who buy before selling pay 20% Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty upfront and get it back only if they sell the flat within 6 months (IRAS).

fplans.note: Main layout per bedroom type (most units where counts are published), redrawn from the developers' plans in the Stacked Homes directory. Score out of 10, same rules for every plan: start at 4; +1 regular shape, dumbbell, kitchen that can be closed off, kitchen or yard window, AC ledge and planter under 5%, store or shelter or utility room; −1 long corridor, ledge and planter 10% or more, balcony over 12%. Efficiency = the share of the area not taken by AC ledges, planters, bay windows and corridors. Plans under the 2023 rules exclude AC ledges from the strata area, so their sq ft is all usable.

concerns: Will too many new condos nearby hurt my price?

Besides this project's own 572 homes, about 968 new homes within 2 km launch within about 2 years of it (Pinery Residences, Bedok Rise (GLS)); the condo resale market within 2 km handles about 94 resales a year. Our test of 33 condos completed 2016 to 2022 in the outer suburbs (11 km or more from the CBD): those with more than 1,817 other new homes completing within 2 km and 2 years grew 4.0% a year over the past 4 years, against 4.3% for those with fewer (URA caveats). Supply nearby is not a big concern here.
The developer paid more for the land. Am I paying more?

Across 16 launches since 2023, launch prices rose roughly dollar for dollar with break-even (about $103 per $100), so developers kept a similar dollar margin while their percentage margin shrank (22% above break-even on land of $1,200 psf ppr or more, 31% on cheaper land). Part of that is location: dearer land is usually where homes sell for more anyway. So a high bid does show up in prices, but only as far as buyers will pay against nearby homes. The test that protects you is the price against same-size competitors: our buy-at and walk-away prices.
Will the developer cut prices later?
100% sold so far. Developers must sell every unit within 5 years of buying the land or repay most of a 40% stamp duty (IRAS); with most units sold, there is little pressure to cut prices.
Should I wait for the next launch nearby?

The next launch nearby, Bedok Rise (GLS), is likely at about $2,300 to $2,700 psf, above this project's 3-bed. Waiting for it is unlikely to get you a cheaper new home here, and a dearer neighbour helps support this project's resale price.

Islandwide, about 18,296 private homes complete in 2027 and 2028 and 15,810 homes in the pipeline were still unsold at mid-2026 (URA). That is enough to keep price growth moderate, but local supply and the local buyer pool matter more for your resale.
